ravi_finance: Heads-up — vendor BalticWare sent invoice INV-4938. Invoice lists VAT ID LT999888777 but the customs docs attached show EORI GB444333222. Vendor has a note: 'Import VAT gross-up applied'. Can AP pay or do we need corrected paperwork?

sara_tax: EORI is for customs transit only, it doesn't substitute a VAT registration. We need the invoicing entity clarified. If the supplier is VAT-registered in Lithuania (LT) they should invoice under LT VAT rules. If the supplier is UK-established and paid import VAT, the invoice must reflect GB VAT details or a reimbursement line.

jo_ops: Vendor says fulfilment from UK hub. They often route via their UK branch. If that's the case the invoice should be from the UK legal entity and show GB VAT number.

taylor_ap: Putting payment on hold until confirmed. What's the minimal ask to avoid repeated reissues?

sara_tax: Request a single corrected PDF that states the legal invoicing entity name and country, the VAT registration with country prefix, and a clear breakout: net amount, VAT (if charged) or 'Import VAT reimbursed' line with amount and currency. Also request supporting docs: VAT registration certificate for the invoicing entity and the customs entry showing EORI used.

nina_legal: If they're passing import VAT as a gross-up, we need an explicit statement that the reimbursed amount only covers import VAT (no other fees) and a confirmation they won't seek additional customs penalties. Prefer a short liability clause in email.

ravi_finance: Drafting message to vendor: "Please reissue invoice INV-4938 to show the correct invoicing entity (name + country) and VAT number with country code. Break out any import VAT reimbursement as a separate line and attach VAT registration proof and customs entry. We will hold payment until we receive the corrected invoice."

invoice-bot: Invoice INV-4938 status: HOLD  tax clarification requested by ravi_finance.

jo_ops: Vendor responded: reissued invoice INV-4938_revA.pdf, now showing GB VAT GB444333222 and a line: 'Import VAT reimbursed to seller: EUR 62.40'. They attached customs entry and a VAT cert for the UK entity.

taylor_ap: Quick checklist: invoice PDF matches PO, vendor legal name matches bank details, currency matches, and separate gross-up line present. If all green we'll process.

sara_tax: Tax note: reimbursing import VAT is fine if documented. We should code this to import_vat_reimb account and keep the customs entry for audit. No VAT to reclaim on our VAT return for that reimbursement.

nina_legal: Update: vendor included a one-line indemnity in their email. Acceptable for now. If gross-up amounts become regular ask for a standard contract addendum.

taylor_ap: All checks passed. Releasing payment today. Marking invoice as PAID in system.

ravi_finance: Thanks team. Closing thread.
